_comment: Generated by crates/kenter-crypto/tests/spend_vectors.rs. Do not hand-edit: regenerate with KENTER_BLESS_VECTORS=1 cargo test -p kenter-crypto --test spend_vectors. kenter-crypto is the source of truth for these bytes.
consumers: keycard-shell — app/crypto/ (C, STM32H5). Builds these messages and hashes them, so the layouts below are its contract.

kenter-keycard — signs the 32-byte digest it is handed and never sees the layout, so it depends on the digest convention here rather than on byte order. Its shared layout is SLIP-0010 derivation: tests/vectors/owner_key_vectors.json.

notes.digest: Owner authorizations sign SHA-256(message), never the message, so a card that can only signHash(32 bytes) produces the same signature as software. See docs/architecture/spend-mode.md.
notes.signatures: Ed25519 is deterministic (RFC 8032), so these are reproducible from the secret alone — a consumer can check its signer, not just its byte layout.

redeem_owner.recipient_note: recipient_xdr is NOT fixed-length and NOT optional. It binds the payout to an address; without it a proof authorises 'redeem this note' rather than 'pay this note to this address', and anyone holding it could redirect the payout. It is `Address::to_xdr`, an ScVal (SCV_ADDRESS, SC_ADDRESS_TYPE_ACCOUNT, PUBLIC_KEY_TYPE_ED25519, key) and 44 bytes for an account, NOT a bare 36-byte account id. Derive it, do not transcribe it.

spend_auth.binding_note: contract_xdr and spend_nonce are both required. The contract address stops an authorisation written for one deployment draining another holding escrow for the same ephemeral key. The nonce makes an authorisation good for exactly one transfer: without it the digest repeats whenever a note returns to a commitment it has held before - and the static pay tag is a reusable address, so change and refunds do exactly that, letting a former payee re-post an old authorisation and take the note back.
